findings.summary: ArXiv is an independent, open-access repository hosting moderated electronic preprints and postprints across physics, mathematics, computer science, and related fields. Founded in 1991 by Paul Ginsparg at Los Alamos National Laboratory, it transitioned to Cornell University in 2001 and became an independent nonprofit in 2026. Authors upload papers after moderation; the platform disseminates research widely before or alongside peer review. It uses the TeX file format for content and supports multiple access methods. ArXiv assigns DOIs via DataCite and tracks submission statistics monthly.

mechanisms.title: Moderated preprint posting
mechanisms.explanation: Authors submit papers which undergo moderation for appropriateness and formatting before being posted to the repository. This process distinguishes arXiv from unmoderated archives and ensures baseline quality control without formal peer review.

mechanisms.title: TeX-based content dissemination
mechanisms.explanation: Papers are submitted in TeX format, a compact typesetting system that enables easy transmission over networks and client-side rendering. This format was foundational to arXiv's creation and remains central to its operation.
